result.title: Let putitoutthere build the npm platform binaries
result.body:
Fixes #12.

## The bug

`@steervec/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu@0.0.3` ships a binary that prints `steervec 0.0.1`.

`CARGO_PKG_VERSION` bakes in at compile time from the on-disk `packages/rust/Cargo.toml`, and nothing in the release run bumps that file before the npm build. `packages/node/scripts/build.mjs:37` cross-compiled the per-target binaries itself, so each published npm binary carries whatever version the crate had at the *previous* release. PyPI was never affected — maturin's `write-version` stamps for it.

## Why the engine wasn't already doing it

`putitoutthere.toml:46` declared `build = [{ mode = "bundled-cli", ... }]` but no `[package.bundle_cli]` block. That block is the gate — without it the reusable workflow skips every bundled-cli step, `write-crate-version` included. The mode declaration alone does nothing.

Stamping from our own script isn't available either: the npm build job passes consumer scripts only `TARGET` and `BUILD`, not the planned version (thekevinscott/putitoutthere#627).

## The fix

Declare the block, delete the cargo branch from `build.mjs`:

```toml
[package.bundle_cli]
bin = "steervec"
crate_path = "packages/rust"
```

Side benefit: Linux rows go through `cargo zigbuild` against a pinned glibc 2.17 floor instead of whatever the runner ships.

The engine stages the binary **flat** at the platform-package root, so two things follow it:

- the launcher passes `binaryDir: ''` (thekevinscott/bin-shim#25, shipped in `0.2.1`; bumped to `^0.2.2`)
- the CI smoke step stages its fake platform package flat too

The flat layout also sidesteps thekevinscott/putitoutthere#626 — with no `bin` directory for `pickMainFile` to choose, `main` lands on the binary and the release-time chmod hits the right inode rather than a directory.

Also drops the pre-committed `optionalDependencies`; the engine rewrites them at publish, so the pinned `0.0.1` entries only ever produced lockfile drift.

## Prior art

Identical change in thekevinscott/agent-transcripts#4, which is released and verified:

```
$ curl -sL .../x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-0.0.3.tgz | tar -tvz
-rwxr-xr-x  906328  package/agent-transcripts
-rw-r--r--     327  package/package.json
$ ./package/agent-transcripts --version
agent-transcripts 0.0.3
```

## Verified here

As far as is possible without cutting a release:

```
$ node packages/node/dist/bin.js --version     # binary staged flat
steervec 0.0.1                                  # local crate version

$ TARGET=x86_64-apple-darwin node scripts/build.mjs
nothing to build for TARGET=x86_64-apple-darwin; the engine stages the binary
```

`typecheck` and `lint` clean. The version stamp itself is only provable by releasing — same as agent-transcripts, where 0.0.3 was the test.

## Note for whoever pulls this

`bin-shim@0.2.2` was published 2026-08-20T21:44:56Z, so any `pnpm install` trips the `minimumReleaseAge` policy until the ~24h cutoff passes. Locally that is `~/.config/pnpm/rc`, and `pnpm --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 ...` works around it. **CI enforces the same policy**: the `build-check` npm rows fail with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`. That clears on its own around 2026-08-21T21:45Z — re-run CI after that rather than chasing the failure.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

           pnpm run build

+      - name: Stage rust binary as platform optional dep (flat, as piot publishes it)
         run: |

 # Changelog
+
+## Unreleased
+
+### Fixed
+
+- The installed binary reported the previous release's version: `steervec@0.0.3`
+  answered `--version` with `steervec 0.0.1`. The per-target binaries were
+  cross-compiled by this package's own build script, which baked
+  `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` in from an unbumped `packages/rust/Cargo.toml`.

+  engine stages and packages it. The launcher passes `binaryDir: ''`, which
+  needs `bin-shim@>=0.2.1`.

+  floor rather than whatever the CI runner ships, widening the range of
+  distributions they run on.

+  publish; the pinned `0.0.1` entries only ever produced lockfile drift.

+
+## Unreleased
+
+### Summary
+
+The npm package shipped a binary that reported the wrong version — `0.0.3`
+answered `--version` with `0.0.1`. Cross-compilation moved from this package's
+build script to putitoutthere's bundled-cli recipe, which stamps the crate
+version before building. Nothing in the package's own API changed.
+
+### Required changes
+
+None.
+
+### Deprecations removed
+
+None.
+
+### Behavior changes without code changes
+
+- `steervec --version` reports the version you installed. Anything that parsed
+  that string to detect the installed release was reading a stale number.
+- Linux binaries now target a glibc 2.17 floor (`cargo zigbuild`), so they run
+  on older distributions than the previous CI-runner-glibc builds did.

+  `@steervec/<triple>/bin/steervec` to `@steervec/<triple>/steervec`. Only
+  affects anything resolving that path directly instead of running the `steervec`
+  bin entry.
+

+
+```
+$ npm install -g steervec
+$ steervec --version
+steervec <the version npm just installed>
+```

   "aarch64-apple-darwin",
   "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc",
 ]

commit.message:
Let putitoutthere build the npm platform binaries

`steervec@0.0.3` ships a binary that answers `--version` with `steervec 0.0.1`.

`CARGO_PKG_VERSION` bakes in at compile time from the on-disk
`packages/rust/Cargo.toml`, and nothing in the release run bumps that file
before the npm build. `packages/node/scripts/build.mjs` did the
cross-compiling itself, so every published npm binary carries the version the
crate had at the previous release. PyPI was always correct — maturin's
`write-version` stamps for it.

`putitoutthere.toml` declared `build = [{ mode = "bundled-cli", ... }]` but no
`[package.bundle_cli]` block, and that block is the gate: without it the
reusable workflow skips every bundled-cli step, `write-crate-version`
included. Stamping from our own script isn't an option — the build job passes
consumer scripts only TARGET and BUILD, not the planned version
(thekevinscott/putitoutthere#627).

So declare the block and delete the cargo branch from build.mjs. Linux rows
also pick up `cargo zigbuild` against a pinned glibc 2.17 floor rather than
whatever the runner ships.

The engine stages the binary flat at the platform-package root, so the
launcher passes `binaryDir: ''` (thekevinscott/bin-shim#25, in 0.2.1) and the
CI smoke step stages its fake platform package the same way. That also
sidesteps thekevinscott/putitoutthere#626: with no `bin` directory to pick,
the engine's `pickMainFile` lands `main` on the binary, so the release-time
chmod hits the right inode instead of a directory.

Drops the pre-committed `optionalDependencies` — the engine rewrites them at
publish, so the pinned `0.0.1` entries only ever produced lockfile drift.

Same change as thekevinscott/agent-transcripts#4, which is released and
verified: `@agent-transcripts/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu@0.0.3` ships a
`-rwxr-xr-x` binary at the tarball root that reports `0.0.3`.

Verified here as far as is possible without cutting a release: the launcher
resolves and runs a flat-staged binary, and a per-triple row is now a no-op.
The version stamp itself is only provable by releasing.

Fixes #12

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

name: Bootstrap npm packages (one-shot)

# One-shot helper to publish 0.0.0-bootstrap stubs for new npm package
# names so the putitoutthere release workflow can publish real versions
# via OIDC trusted publishing afterwards. npm trusted publishing binds
# to an already-published package, so the first publish needs a classic
# token; this workflow is the bootstrap path.
#
# Usage:
#   1. Create a granular npm automation token (read+write, short expiry)
#      and set it as repo secret NPM_TOKEN.
#   2. gh workflow run bootstrap-npm.yml -f packages="name1,name2,..."
#   3. Once stubs land, register Trusted Publishers on each package's
#      npm settings page pointing at this repo + release.yml + the
#      "pypi" environment.
#   4. Delete the NPM_TOKEN secret.
#   5. Re-trigger Release; the engine publishes real versions over the
#      bootstrap stubs via OIDC.
#
# This file can be removed once all steervec + @steervec/*
# npm names exist on the registry — its only job is the first-publish
# bootstrap.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      packages:
        description: 'Comma-separated list of npm package names to bootstrap'
        required: true

jobs:
  bootstrap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - name: Publish bootstrap stubs
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.packages }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IFS=',' read -ra PKGS <<< "$PACKAGES"
          for name in "${PKGS[@]}"; do
            name="${name// /}"
            echo "::group::publish 0.0.0-bootstrap for $name"
            dir=$(mktemp -d)
            pushd "$dir" > /dev/null
            cat > package.json <<EOF
          {
            "name": "$name",
            "version": "0.0.0-bootstrap",
            "description": "Bootstrap stub; replaced on first real publish via OIDC trusted publisher.",
            "license": "MIT",
            "repository": {
              "type": "git",
              "url": "git+https://github.com/thekevinscott/steervec.git"
            }
          }
          EOF
            # --tag bootstrap: 0.0.0-bootstrap is a prerelease (hyphen),
            # which npm refuses to publish as `latest`. Tag it explicitly
            # so the real 0.0.1 publish is the one that becomes `latest`.
            npm publish --access public --tag bootstrap
            popd > /dev/null
            rm -rf "$dir"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

name: Changelog

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  enforce:
    name: CHANGELOG + MIGRATIONS touched
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Check
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Bypass when any commit on the PR carries a `skip-changelog:` trailer.
          if git log --format=%B "$BASE_SHA..$HEAD_SHA" \
            | grep -Eiq '^skip-changelog:'; then
            echo "skip-changelog trailer present; bypassing enforcement."
            exit 0
          fi

          changed=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA")

          packages=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" \
            | awk -F/ '$1 == "packages" && NF >= 2 { print $2 }' \
            | sort -u)

          if [ -z "$packages" ]; then
            echo "No package files touched; nothing to enforce."
            exit 0
          fi

          fail=0
          for pkg in $packages; do
            touched_code=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" \
              | grep -E "^packages/${pkg}/" \
              | grep -Ev "^packages/${pkg}/(CHANGELOG|MIGRATIONS)\.md$" \
              | grep -Ev "^packages/${pkg}/.*\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx|js|py|rs)$" \
              | grep -Ev "^packages/${pkg}/(tests?|__tests__)/" \
              || true)

            if [ -z "$touched_code" ]; then
              continue
            fi

            for f in CHANGELOG.md MIGRATIONS.md; do
              if ! printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep -qx "packages/${pkg}/${f}"; then
                echo "::error file=packages/${pkg}/${f}::packages/${pkg} has code changes but ${f} is not updated. Add an entry under '## Unreleased' or include a 'skip-changelog:' trailer for genuinely internal refactors."
                fail=1
              fi
            done
          done

          exit $fail

name: Docs

on:

          version: 10.33.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

name: Node

on:

      - 'packages/node/**'
      - 'packages/rust/**'
      - '.github/workflows/node.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/node
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10.33.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm run lint

  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/node
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10.33.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm run typecheck

  build:
    name: Build + smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10.33.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Build rust binary
        run: cargo build --release
        working-directory: packages/rust
      - name: Build node package
        run: |
          pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
          pnpm run build
        working-directory: packages/node
      - name: Stage rust binary as platform optional dep (flat, as piot publishes it)
        run: |
          pkg=@steervec/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          target=packages/node/node_modules/$pkg
          mkdir -p "$target"
          printf '{"name":"%s","version":"0.0.1"}\n' "$pkg" > "$target/package.json"
          install -m 755 packages/rust/target/release/steervec "$target/steervec"
      - name: Smoke (--version via node wrapper -> rust binary)
        run: node packages/node/dist/bin.js --version

name: PR Monitor

on:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  # A superseded gate run polls a stale SHA until it finishes. Cancel it.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  # willfire reads the PR and its changed files to predict which workflows dispatch.
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  monitor:
    name: 'CI Gate'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The action has no timeout of its own (see monitor.ts) -- this is the
    # backstop. If a predicted run never dispatches, the gate waits here
    # until the job is killed.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: thekevinscott/pr-monitor@v1

name: Python

on:

      - 'packages/rust/**'
      - '.github/workflows/python.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build wheel + smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ['3.9', '3.10', '3.11', '3.12', '3.13']
    steps:

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

        with:

      - name: Build wheel

          .venv/bin/steervec --version

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  release:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    secrets:
      # First publish of a brand-new crate has no Trusted Publishing path
      # on crates.io (TP binds to an already-published crate). Forward a
      # long-lived API token; the reusable workflow skips the OIDC
      # exchange when this secret is set. Once 0.0.1 is on crates.io,
      # register a Trusted Publisher and unset this.
      CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
      # Same first-publish bootstrap for npm: TP binds to an already-
      # published package, so the very first publish needs a long-lived
      # token. The reusable workflow exports this to NODE_AUTH_TOKEN
      # for the npm CLI when set. Once all 6 packages exist on the
      # registry (steervec + 5 @steervec/<triple> sub-packages), register
      # Trusted Publishers per package and unset this secret.
      NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

  # PyPI upload runs in the caller's workflow context. Required because
  # PyPI Trusted Publishers can't validate OIDC tokens minted from a
  # cross-repo reusable workflow (pypi/warehouse#11096). The `if:` gate
  # skips this job for non-PyPI repos.
  pypi-publish:
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.has_pypi == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-sdist'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-wheel-*'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

name: Rust

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'packages/rust/**'
      - '.github/workflows/rust.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint (fmt + clippy)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

  unit:
    name: Unit tests + coverage (95%)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: cargo llvm-cov --ignore-filename-regex 'main\.rs' --fail-under-lines 95

  build:
    name: Build + smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      - run: cargo build --release
      - name: Smoke (--version)
        run: ./target/release/steervec --version
